title: Live symbol-stitching patch manager to reduce GPU restart blast radius
creator: Marcus Nguyen
description:
Problem: Upgrading CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS artifacts in the field often requires full process restarts or rolling nodes out of service when symbol mismatches occur. Restarts create latency spikes and reduce capacity during upgrades and emergency rollbacks.

Goal: Implement a lightweight runtime component ("Live Symbol-Stitcher") that can apply small binary-level relocations and symbol redirections at process scope to resolve common symbol ABI mismatches without a full GPU-serving process restart. This reduces blast radius for dependency upgrades and enables faster canary roll-forward/rollback cycles.

Scope:
- Design a safe, audited mechanism to patch/unpatch symbol bindings for a restricted set of known symbols used by GEMM and quant kernels (entry points and dispatch shims).
- Integrate with our canary pipeline so stitch operations can be gated by end-to-end canary success metrics.
- Add telemetry: successful stitch count, time-to-stitch, failures and auto-revert triggers.
- Provide a developer/debug CLI and an operator API (read-only for hosted, writable for Dedicated/Private with RBAC).

Non-goals:
- Not implementing a full hot-patching framework for arbitrary binary edits. Not attempting to rewrite kernel logic at runtime.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Demonstrable reduction in required node restarts for three upgrade scenarios (CUTLASS minor bump, Triton patch, CUDA driver minor version) validated on staging.
2) Canary gating: a failed stitch must auto-revert within X minutes and emit an alert.
3) Operator tooling: patch apply/verify/revert commands + audit log entries for every operation.
4) Performance: stitch application must complete within 30s for typical nodes and not cause sustained token latency regressions >5%.

Risks & Mitigations:
- Risk: incorrect relocation could corrupt process state. Mitigation: run stitch in a sandboxed inspector process that validates symbol integrity and runs smoke kernels before committing.
- Risk: security surface area. Mitigation: require signature verification for stitch bundles and restrict write API to enterprise RBAC roles.

Rollout plan:
1) Prototype low-risk symbol remapping on staging with non-critical dispatcher symbols.
2) Add automatic canary tests (small synthetic workloads + perf/accuracy checks).
3) Deploy to Dedicated canary pool under opt-in; collect telemetry for 2 weeks.
4) Expand symbol coverage and enable in hosted behind feature flag and strict audit logging.
